issues.what: After the third perk reveals, the next four sampled frames show the same page state while the cursor crosses the hero toward Apply. There is no new beat for roughly six seconds before the click setup.
issues.fix: Keep one short hold to read the final perk, then take the cursor directly to Apply so the first application step follows without the long traverse.

issues.what: The close-up isolates the ball, cursor and round bumper, but clips the feature name at the bottom and removes the nearby lane, so the shot does not establish what the ball has reached.
issues.fix: Pull back and shift the close-up to include the complete Background Check sign and a short stretch of approach lane while keeping the ball and bumper central.

issues.where: first jump between localized pinball views, 1:16.13–1:17.93
issues.what: The view jumps from the Background Check field to a similarly framed Corporate HQ field. With the outer table and the path between fields out of frame, the ball looks as if it teleports between two versions of the same board.
issues.fix: Bridge the switch with a brief wider follow of the ball, or carry the shared exit and entry lanes across the two close shots to establish how the fields connect.

issues.what: The same full-page view holds while dialogs, error tiles, the timer and the moving Submit button compete in separate parts of the frame. Several consecutive samples repeat the same setup without a clear new cause and effect.
issues.fix: Stagger the obstructions so each has a readable trigger and response, trim the repeated chase poses, and return attention to the active Submit button before the mechanism breaks apart.

issues.what: The verification card is anchored upper left, but the primary Submit button sits on its own near the bottom center across a large blank area. The at-rest page has no clear visual path from the checkbox to its next action.
issues.fix: Put the at-rest Submit button in a footer aligned to the verification card or immediately below it. Let its escape animation move it away from that predictable starting point.

issues.what: The error tile sits directly over the email field, masking the value the viewer needs to compare with the correction.
issues.fix: Place the error immediately below or beside the field in reserved space so the error and the entered value are visible together.
